card.title: Waiting for the Bad News
card.instruction: Treat pauses, changes, and uncertainty as signs that rejection or loss is approaching, then prepare yourself before it arrives.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You moved our meeting to Friday. I've brought a box for my desk.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's a promotion. You'll manage the new branch.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Away from everyone? I'll pack before they have to say goodbye.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You can still come to Friday drinks.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll bring my own glass. Better get used to being a visitor before they stop inviting me.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 prepares a desk box after a meeting change, A3 treats promotion away as impending loss, and A5 rehearses visitor status before imagined exclusion.

responseLogic.evidence: B2's branch promotion informs A3's packing-for-goodbye plan; B4's drinks invitation becomes A5's bring-own-glass preparation.

relationship.evidence: B2 provides positive employment news and B4 offers a concrete way to keep the old social connection.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4's continued invitation to prepare for a future when invitations stop.

specificity.evidence: A1 establishes a moved meeting and feared desk departure; B2 states the actual promotion.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's own-glass choice makes anticipatory loss visible through B4's drinks offer.
